title: Pipeline Order
similar: LeetCode 210 Course Schedule II (lexicographically smallest variant)
hints: Which stages can run first? What changes when one of them finishes?
Keep a count of unfinished prerequisites per stage. A stage with count 0 is ready. Finishing a stage lowers the counts of the stages that need it.
Kahn's algorithm, but keep the ready stages in a min-heap so you always run the smallest label. If fewer than n stages ever became ready, there is a cycle: print -1.

wrong.fifo_queue.cpp: uses a plain FIFO queue of ready stages, so the order is valid but not the smallest
wrong.no_cycle_check.cpp: prints whatever order it produced, even when a cycle left some stages unscheduled
wrong.tle_scan_ready.cpp: scans all n stages for the smallest ready one at every step (fails the perf group)

strategy.question: Scout the statement: n up to 2*10^5 stages, m dependencies, 'smallest valid order or -1'. Which plan fits?
options: Try all permutations and keep the first valid one
DFS from stage 1 and print the visit order
Count unfinished prerequisites; repeatedly run the smallest ready stage from a min-heap; -1 if some stage never becomes ready
Sort the stages by how many prerequisites they have
strategy.why: Permutations are n!. A plain DFS visit order ignores dependencies. Sorting by prerequisite count is not enough (a stage with 1 prerequisite can still need a late one). Kahn's algorithm with a min-heap schedules the smallest ready label each step in O((n+m) log n), and a cycle shows up as stages that never reach count 0.
